extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of English literature; educated general readers interested in Shakespeare and Elizabethan England
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on reconstructing and presenting the life and times of William Shakespeare using contemporary documents, publication records, and oral traditions, with attention to historical context and inference methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facts established by contemporary documents first
rubrics_metrics.description: In a matter which has been the subject of so much controversy, it may be an aid to clearness if the facts established by contemporary documents be first related, and the less trustworthy reports added later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authoritative principle: present facts provable from contemporary documents before introducing oral traditions or later reports. Use documents to anchor the narrative and clearly separate them from conjecture or tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on official records; supplement with oral traditions when records are sparse
rubrics_metrics.description: The preservation of official records makes it possible for the modern scholar to reconstruct with considerable fullness the careers of public men; but in the case of Shakespeare ... we must needs be content with a few scrappy documents, supplemented by oral traditions of varying degrees of authenticity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological standard: prioritize official, archival records (baptismal registers, court rolls, Stationers' entries, Treasurer's accounts) for reconstruction; where records are limited, clearly qualify and contextualize use of oral tradition and later anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer vital dates from contemporaneous practices (e.g., baptism timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The monument over his grave states that at his death on April 23, 1616, he was 'Ætatis 53,' which would seem to indicate that he must have been born at least as early as April 22; and, since in those days baptism usually took place within a very few days of birth, there is no reason for pushing the date farther back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical inference rule: use standard contemporary practices (such as rapid baptism after birth) to make cautious chronological inferences from surviving records (e.g., baptismal entries) while acknowledging uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret dedications and publication terms in their historical context
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms of the dedication, which is to the Earl of Southampton, ... do not imply any close relation between poet and patron; and the phrase 'the first heyre of my invention' need not be taken as placing its composition earlier than any of the plays, since writing for the stage was then scarcely regarded as practising the art of letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hermeneutic guideline: read dedications, prefatory remarks, and publication language against contemporaneous conventions rather than assuming modern meanings (e.g., a flattering dedication may not indicate intimacy; 'first heir of my invention' may not date composition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contemporary literary allusions and pamphlet references as evidence of reputation and authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Greene's upstart-crow passage and Chettle's prefatory remarks are treated as contemporary allusions that likely refer to Shakespeare and indicate his dual profession as actor and author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical practice: evaluate anonymous or oblique contemporary references (pamphlets, quartos, addresses) as evidentiary when wording, tone, and context align; cite the specific passages (e.g., Greene's 'upstart crow' and Chettle's appraisal) as support, but note degrees of certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat publication records and frequency of editions as indicators of literary distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: The frequency of complimentary references to these poems, and the number of editions issued during the poet's lifetime (seven of Venus, and five of Lucrece), indicate that it was through them that he first obtained literary distinction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stationers' records, registration dates, dedications, and the number of contemporary editions as corroborating evidence for dating works and assessing contemporary popularity and reputation.
